# Dev

`<package>` in this skill and its linked files is this root. If the value above
is not an absolute path, the root is two directories above this `SKILL.md`.

Read the [framework](../../README.md). This is a start/resume entry, not a worker
stage or a second workflow controller. Claude's packaged command is
`/kc-dev-flow-2:dev`; bare `/dev` is not a promised cross-host alias.

Resolve the absolute project root, explicit workflow directory and intended work
item from the request and authoritative project/task records. Reuse established
context; do not guess between projects or tasks. Read applicable project
conventions and the existing context needed for the requested work.

After resolving the code root, run `python3 <package>/scripts/learning.py --repo
<absolute-code-root> notices --all`. Present relevant unread learning results (items
with `unread` true) to the user, distinguishing pending/uncertain, no-change, local proposal, PR and observed
merge; pending proposals are not active rules. Only after actual presentation,
run `ack --job <job> --expected <notice_digest>` for each shown snapshot. Context
injection or reading alone is not presentation. A changed digest stays unread;
interruption may repeat a notice. Settle every delivery shown `open`, acknowledged or not, by reading its PR
with `gh pr view` as learn's `Follow the delivery to a recorded end` says, before presenting.
Read failure holds that learning action, not
unrelated approved development. This entry-level check is not a host SessionStart
hook. Use [learn](../learn/SKILL.md) for an explicitly requested named-task loop;
notices do not authorize evaluation, delivery, retry or merge.

For existing work, preserve its recorded variant/profile, approved outcome,
scope, non-goals and stop condition. Read current state, reports and delivery
status instead of assuming a prior conversation is current. An invalid profile,
conflicting records or missing authority holds the dependent action; return only
the unresolved decision to the user. Do not restart approved design or ask again
for an unchanged selection.

For new work without a profile selection, establish the intended outcome and
recommend a profile using the framework's intended use and applicable shared
profile principles. Ask the user to select it before profile-dependent work.
An explicit valid selection is sufficient; FO records it with the variant in
the work item through the existing workflow. Recommendation is not selection.
For new work that adds a capability no journey map holds, ask once, before recommending a profile, whether to draw a story map first with kc-journey-map (`map`, `plan-release`, then `review-release`, which interrogates the release before splitting it). Record the result on each task as the workflow's `Release review:` line, or `Release review: not needed: <his words>`.

Hand the resolved project root, explicit workflow directory, work item, approved
selection/scope and bounded outcome to `spacedock:first-officer`, with this
skill's `Package root:` value, which FO writes into the scope notes of every
worker dispatch and follow-up message with a line telling the worker to send its completion
message to `main`, because the completion block Spacedock appends names `team-lead`. Retain that
workflow directory as `--workflow-dir` on SD commands; cwd alone is not the
binding. If FO is already active, continue there. SD owns stage selection, live
worker availability, dispatch, reports, gates and recovery; a resumed FO does
not establish that its old worker still exists. An entity sitting in a stage
declared `gate: true` is excluded from `spacedock status --next` and from
`--boot`'s DISPATCHABLE table before the concurrency check runs (Spacedock
v0.27.0, `internal/status/format.go`, `dispatchAnalysis`, reason `gate`), so an
empty dispatchable view does not mean no worker is available; three of this
workflow's five stages (`backlog`, `ideation`, `validation`) declare `gate: true`,
so that empty view is this workflow's normal case, not the exception. Stage
skills own profile routing and load the selected references in each worker's
context.

Before each worker dispatch and on resume, run `python3 <package>/scripts/workflow_checkout.py
<workflow-dir>/README.md`. Exit 1 means the README FO follows differs from the trunk's,
exit 2 that it could not be compared; hold the dispatch, show the Captain the printed
remedy or cause, and wait. Do not run the remedy or move the checkout yourself. This
sentence sits here because a README old enough to be wrong may not contain it.

If adoption is absent or the selected profile does not match the ordered stage
graph, follow the [SD adoption reference](../../references/sd/adoption.md) through
`spacedock:commission` or `spacedock:refit` before dispatch. Invoking this entry does
not migrate an old variant, rewrite a workflow or install a package. Keep existing
work on its recorded variant unless a migration is explicitly approved. This
entry grants no new repair, approval, delivery or route-exception authority.

48	
49	# Development workflow
50	<!-- kc-dev-flow-2 0.33.1 x-release-please-version -->
51	
52	This is the adopted workflow's authority for SD stages and task schema. Resolve
53	its absolute directory and retain `--workflow-dir` on SD commands, including
54	worker reads and recovery. Skills guide work; SD owns dispatch, gates and state.
55	
56	## File Naming
57	
58	Each task is a flat `<slug>.md` file in the resolved state checkout. Keep existing
59	IDs and tasks in their recorded workflow; new work does not migrate old work.
60	
61	## Schema
62	
63	Record `title`, `status`, `variant: kc-dev-flow-2`, and the user's selected
64	`profile`; `id` is optional under `id-style: slug`. The five-stage route accepts
65	`pilot` or `prod`; the POC adaptation
66	removes ideation from both frontmatter and Stages and accepts `poc` only.
67	Before admission and dispatch, FO holds unknown/mismatched profiles;
68	SD does not enforce this rule. Preserve approved outcome and scope.
69	New seeds require non-empty `Non-goals:`, `Budget:` and `Stop condition:` lines
70	under `## Scope` or matching level-two sections. Replay counts do not enforce
71	these on existing tasks. Use bold **AC-N** declarations with individual evidence clauses.
72	
73	## Batch gates
74	
75	A Captain-approved batch covers one release slice or theme. Recover members from accepted scopes/questions, without another list. Unclear membership holds presentation; membership changes or splits need his decision. Incompatible stage graphs need an explicitly approved split.
76	
77	At each next gate, wait for every member's sufficient committed evidence, then present the batch in one sitting. Early finishers prompt no decision. Continue authorized repairs/validation. A blocker needing Captain authority gets one exception question naming the member and effect. Do not manufacture hold resolutions.
78	
79	`<package>/scripts/pr_watch.py tasks` sitting hints remain subject to this boundary; stage alone joins neither unrelated tasks nor incomplete batches. Unbatched tasks retain ordinary gates.
80	
81	When requested, chief-engineer reviews the complete package/process batch before briefing bindings; engineering-reviewer handles contested hard-to-reverse claims. Give committed task files/artifact links, not FO's suspicions/conclusions. Record reviewer/model/evidence; use a different family from all workers or ask the Captain. Review advises, without approval authority.
82	
83	## Stages
84	
85	Stage workers run on the workflow's default model.
86	`kc-dev-flow-2:chief-engineer`, `kc-dev-flow-2:engineering-reviewer` and
87	`kc-dev-flow-2:observer` run on the model and reasoning their agent files declare, never
88	a cheaper one. Record chief-engineer and engineering-reviewer calls under `## FO alignment` as
89	`Reviewer: <agent> <model> <date> — <question>`; `<package>/scripts/role_triggers.py` lists calls owed.
90	
91	`concurrency` limits only what `status --next` proposes. A feedback-reflow repair and an
92	FO fix authorized under Review-finding disposition step 3 are dispatched at once in the
93	entity's own worktree, after the existing overlap check against running worktrees; they
94	do not wait for another entity's worker in the same stage. The validation recheck of
95	that repair or fix does not wait for another entity's worker either, but it is
96	dispatched only after the repair or fix has completed and committed its candidate, so
97	the validator reads the bytes that will be delivered. A repair that outgrows what its
98	assignment names returns to FO as a scope change.
99	
100	FO resolves `<package>` in this workflow from the `Package root:` line of
101	`kc-dev-flow-2:dev`. Before each worker dispatch FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/package_version.py
102	<this README>`; exit 1 means the session loaded an older package than this README was synced
103	from, and FO holds the dispatch until the session runs the newer one. FO also runs
104	`python3 <package>/scripts/workflow_checkout.py <this README>`, which compares this file with
105	`origin/<trunk>`'s: exit 1 means they differ, exit 2 that it could not compare, and FO
106	holds the dispatch and shows the Captain what the script printed. Every worker dispatch FO builds carries that absolute path as a
107	`Package root: <absolute path>` line in its scope notes (`--scope-notes-file`), which
108	land in the dispatch file the worker reads first. Those scope notes, and every follow-up
109	message to a live worker, also carry ``Send your completion message to `main` (the README's Dispatch
110	facts: `team-lead` is not registered here).``: the builder's completion block names `team-lead`, and a
111	worker that skips the stage-definition fetch does not see the Signal fact. FO saves those scope notes, the
112	checklist, the model it dispatches on and the SHA it dispatches from as
113	`<task>/dispatch/<stage>-<cycle>.md` in the state checkout (for validation a
114	`Candidate: <full head SHA>` line per head validated),
115	committed with that dispatch's `spacedock state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`, so
116	the instruction a worker followed outlives the session that wrote it; FO runs
117	`python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py <task folder>` before committing and fixes each part it lists. A follow-up
118	message to a worker FO resumes is a dispatch too, with the same check and a checklist of the items that message asks, never a pointer to another record.
119	After each worker report, before advancing or preparing its gate, FO runs
120	`python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py --coverage <task> --stage <stage>`; nonzero holds that task.
121	This check does not observe unrecorded messages.
122	A checklist or scope-notes line that names a package script writes
123	`<package>/scripts/NAME.py` with the absolute root substituted, never the bare script
124	name; before `dispatch build`, FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py --names <record>`
125	on the saved record and rewrites each name it lists. When `status --set` refuses to leave a stage, run `spacedock status --workflow-dir
126	<dir> --read <task> --stage <stage> --checklist`, return any line it reports as neither
127	DONE nor SKIPPED to the worker with the request to append a complete new report under the same heading, ending in a Summary that supersedes the earlier one, and do not edit the worker's report. The refusal itself
128	does not say why; other causes are a missing evidence line or Summary and an uncommitted
129	report.
130	
131	### `backlog`
132	
133	The user selects the compatible profile and approves outcome, scope and budget.
134	FO records the choice; this boundary has no worker or placeholder report. FO
135	also records, under a `## FO alignment` heading in the task file, whether FO
136	direction alignment with the Captain is needed before the next declared stage
137	and why; a
138	stated reason is the whole record when not needed. On the five-stage route, FO
139	also records a `Surfaces:` line under the same heading: any of `ui`, `db`,
140	or `none`, read from the change surface rather than the diff, and next to it
141	a `Visible change:` line: one sentence on what a user sees or operates
142	differently, or `Visible change: none`.
143	
144	- **Gate content:** Show the selected variant/profile, proposed outcome, scope,
145	  exclusions and evidence needed before the next declared stage starts, the
146	  `## FO alignment` need and reason, and the recorded `Surfaces:` and
147	  `Visible change:` lines on the five-stage route.
148	- **Seed check:** On the five-stage route, before `gate prepare`, FO runs
149	  `python3 <package>/scripts/design_surfaces.py check --seed <task>` and holds the
150	  gate until it exits 0. An FO that skips this step still dispatches; no runtime hook blocks it.
151	- **Release review:** Applies to a task that belongs to a release on a journey map
152	  (`journey`, `journey-release`, `journey-story`); a task with no release, such as a
153	  bug, infrastructure or workflow maintenance, is outside it. Four signals: (1) a task
154	  admitted into a release; (2) a Captain scope ruling that moves a story or task into
155	  or out of a release or changes the goal of the release, a story or a task; (3) a UAT
156	  failure that crosses two or more tasks; (4) a batch about to enter implementation. Signals 1 and 2 only mark the
157	  release changed: FO names the release and the signal in the task's `## FO alignment`
158	  reason. A task whose `journey-story` is already on the map in that release passes with
159	  that one check and marks nothing when, since its latest `Release review:` line, the
160	  journey file still holds the same story ids and the same release and story `goal`
161	  text and no Captain ruling has changed the goal of the release, a story or a task.
162	  A changed goal is signal 2 although no story id moved; FO marks the release
163	  changed in that task's `## FO alignment` reason. Signal 4 is the single checkpoint: at the first
164	  implementation dispatch for a release marked changed, FO dispatches a fresh worker
165	  with kc-journey-map's `review-release` mode, then splits tasks from its output; an
166	  unchanged release proceeds. One review covers every change since the last. Signal 3
167	  runs the review at once. FO writes no map and no candidate; the Captain accepts
168	  membership in conversation or at this gate. FO records under `## FO alignment` either
169	  `Release review: <journey>/<release-id> at <journey-file commit>` or
170	  `Release review: not needed: <reason>`. When FO approves
171	  a task into a release story at this gate it sets the three fields with
172	  `spacedock status --workflow-dir <dir> --set <task> journey=<the map's journey: value> journey-release=<id> journey-story=<id>`;
173	  a worker never edits frontmatter. Where the adopter tracks completion with
174	  kc-journey-progress, FO also writes `journey-required-tasks` (full task ids) and
175	  `journey-mapping-complete: true` on one task per story at the review's split step.
176	  When signal 2 moves a task out of a release, FO clears its release fields with
177	  `spacedock status --workflow-dir <dir> --set <task> journey= journey-release= journey-story= journey-required-tasks= journey-mapping-complete=`
178	  (a field set to nothing is cleared). Where kc-journey-progress is tracking, follow its
179	  skill for the lists; when the cleared task was the declaring one, FO moves that list and
180	  `journey-mapping-complete: true` to another member of the story. kc-journey-progress
181	  reports a story unverified until its declaration matches its members.
182	
183	### `ideation`
184	
185	FO may dispatch ideation on a stronger model when the design is hard to reverse,
186	such as an event model, an architecture or a security boundary, and says so in
187	the dispatch. The default ensign invokes `kc-dev-flow-2:ideation` before useful work, using the
188	work item's recorded variant/profile and the skill's own profile routing table.
189	FO aligns direction and requests research when it can change a decision; the
190	worker authors the PRFAQ and the artifact each recorded surface owes. When
191	`## FO alignment` records alignment as needed, FO records the alignment result
192	as a `Result:` line before dispatching the worker. Missing skill or profile
193	authority requires a hold report rather than a baseline or default-profile
194	substitution.
195	Ideation writes no repository file, branch or commit: the design, the criteria and any
196	ADR draft live in the task file, and a draft carries no ADR number.
197	
198	- **Outputs:** Current design definition and acceptance criteria with reproducible
199	  evidence clauses; unresolved decisions identified for the user.
200	- **Gate content:** Present PRFAQ/Mermaid with matching actors, order, branches,
201	  approvals and stops, acceptance evidence/limits, and each recorded
202	  `Surfaces:` value's artifact. The gate is not presentable without the
203	  artifact each recorded surface owes. Before `spacedock gate prepare`, FO runs
204	  `python3 <package>/scripts/design_surfaces.py check <task>`, includes its
205	  output in the gate material at any exit, and treats a non-zero exit as the gate
206	  not presentable. Required diagram defects or missing current-stage
207	  evidence block recommendation and gate preparation/presentation; honest
208	  unverified future checks do not.
209	  FO may correct design prose/Mermaid to reflect established decisions under an
210	  actual Captain grant covering that task's exact design section; reuse a matching
211	  standing grant. Template adoption grants no authority. Record the decision basis;
212	  preserve scope, acceptance criteria, risk acceptance, product code, worker
213	  evidence, prior reports, approvals and verdicts. Withdraw an affected open binding
214	  before editing, then reprepare through the applicable SD lifecycle. Other
215	  corrections require an authorized author; hold where no supported route applies,
216	  without inventing same-stage rework. Corrections neither replace user approval nor advance stages.
217	
218	### `implementation`
219	
220	The default ensign invokes `kc-dev-flow-2:implementation` before useful work,
221	using the recorded profile and approved scope. Produce the bounded integrated
222	result and its evidence. Missing inputs require a hold; scope/profile changes
223	return to the affected user decision. Apply Review-finding disposition to repairs;
224	a repair is dispatched under the lane in Stages.
225	
226	- **Outputs:** Exact delivered artifact, checks actually run, and material limits
227	  recorded in the existing SD Stage Report.
228	
229	### `validation`
230	
231	A fresh ensign invokes `kc-dev-flow-2:validation` before useful work and checks
232	the exact artifact against the accepted profile outcome. It assesses the work;
233	it does not silently take over implementation. Rejection uses the supported
234	feedback path after the distinct FO disposition described below. Its recheck of a
235	repair is dispatched under the lane in Stages.
236	
237	- **Outputs:** Independent verdict, primary evidence, a minimal acceptance script, the
238	  `python3 <package>/scripts/adr_lint.py docs/adr --since <base>` command run with its exit
239	  code, and unverified obligations recorded in the existing SD Stage Report.
240	- **Gate content:** Show actual checks and acceptance evidence, material findings
241	  and limits, and the user's pending delivery decision. For a `ui` task FO runs
242	  `python3 <package>/scripts/design_surfaces.py check <task>` and includes its
243	  output. Before the gate, FO runs the
244	  stage's minimal acceptance script exactly as written in a fresh shell, then presents
245	  every step in full beside its observed output, never a pointer or a shortened step.
246	  A step FO cannot run (a secret, a sign-in, the Captain's own device) is marked not
247	  run with the reason; an output that differs from the script returns through feedback.
248	  Before recommending delivery, FO confirms both goal sufficiency and minimal
249	  necessity from the same candidate's existing route evidence. Passing checks or
250	  approval replace neither condition; approval is not merge. When a POC report
251	  records `boundary-crossed:`, FO shows the marker and its evidence with the
252	  user's choice between profile selection and removing the crossing work with
253	  recorded cleanup through the feedback route, and does not recommend
254	  delivering that work as POC.
255	
256	### `done`
257	
258	Consuming a terminal gate approval is not completion (`spacedock merge guard --help`);
259	a live run requires the declared delivery evidence and successful `merge guard` with
260	an explicit verdict. Apply Delivery authority below; a pending PR or missing hook is
261	not completion.
262	
263	## Dispatch facts
264	
265	- **Team:** You are one worker in a team completing the project goal; your stage
266	  and handoff serve that goal. Before substantial work or retrying a failure,
267	  check this task's prior reports, linked sibling tasks and PRs, and relevant
268	  workflow state: did someone already do this, hit this, or own it now? If your
269	  environment cannot run a required checklist check, tell FO before building
270	  work that depends on it. Ask FO early about overlapping ownership, repeated
271	  failures, missing authority or evidence, or infeasible targets. Give checked
272	  sources, findings, attempts and the specific question. With a mid-run FO
273	  channel, pause dependent work and continue safe independent work; without
274	  one, end your turn with that handback instead of waiting. Never answer your
275	  own or your reviewers' permission requests; route them to FO. FO coordinates
276	  peers and decisions; do not message peers or change others' work.
277	- **Signal:** send the completion message once, to the first officer by the name
278	  your session lists as addressable (`main` under Claude Code dispatch). The
279	  completion block's `team-lead` is Spacedock's default and is not registered
280	  there (spacedock-dev/spacedock #523, #608); do not try it first and do not
281	  describe a fallback in the report.
282	- **Package:** `<package>` in stage text is the `Package root:` line of the
283	  kc-dev-flow-2 skill you loaded; your dispatch's scope notes state the same path,
284	  and if they differ, use the skill's. Run package scripts only from it; never
285	  search the filesystem, `/tmp` or another install for them.
286	- **Secrets:** `<wrapper>` is the only route to a development secret: run a
287	  command that needs one as `<wrapper> <command>`. Never read or print a value.
288	  If a guard refuses a command that only mentions a secret-reading tool, rephrase
289	  it; do not split, encode or wrap the command to pass the guard.
290	
291	## Review-finding disposition
292	
293	Before repair authorization, product bytes and the recorded candidate revision stay
294	unchanged. Read-only inspection, non-mutating reproductions, existing tests and
295	throwaway-checkout probes are allowed. Report/gate commits may advance repository
296	HEAD without changing the candidate. Validators recommend `PASSED` or `REJECTED`;
297	new findings or changed evidence re-enter this checkpoint.
298	
299	The four evidence fields are released user and normal workflow; observable harm;
300	affected value acceptance criterion or non-negotiable boundary; and trigger
301	evidence. Field 3 uses `value-ac[AC-N]`, `captain-ruling[YYYY-MM-DD]`, or
302	`contract[repo/relative/path#anchor]` plus a nonblank claim. `none:` with a rationale
303	does not establish Material.
304	
305	- **Material:** all four fields establish supported-workflow harm to a protected
306	  boundary or value acceptance criterion.
307	- **Deferred risk:** hypothetical, unsupported, unobserved or unpromised trigger;
308	  record what would make it material.
309	- **Polish:** no current user-visible loss or protected boundary is at risk.
310	- **Needs decision:** the task cannot own the scope, product or compatibility call.
311	
312	A `Follow-up:` line in Scope is not accepted scope by itself: the first stage of the
313	receiving task to meet it assesses it against its stated reason and earlier rulings. It builds the line only when the change alters no behaviour that an
314	accepted criterion, a Captain ruling or a journey contract relies on; otherwise it
315	returns the line to FO as a Needs decision. It records which, and why.
316	A finding FO declined in a committed gate summary or under `### FO declines` is settled:
317	a later validator does not report it again unless the candidate changes the lines or the
318	evidence the decline names, or new evidence would make it Material.
319	
320	## FO steps: review findings
321	
322	Apply this checkpoint to findings from implementation, validation, detached audits,
323	consequential FO quick work and rejected gates.
324	
325	1. Reviewers observe; workers' classifications and `actor:ensign` Resolutions are
326	   advisory. Preserve findings and assess the four evidence fields above, separating
327	   materiality, ownership and disposition. Missing required evidence or unresolved
328	   classification requires investigation or hold.
329	2. Within approved boundaries, FO may explicitly decline evidenced Deferred risk or
330	   Polish in the existing committed gate summary, naming the finding, reason, candidate
331	   revision and the lines or evidence it rests on. When that summary is already
332	   consumed, FO writes the decline under `### FO declines` in the task file, committed
333	   with `spacedock state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`, and the terminal gate
334	   lists each entry there. This FO-authored decision requires no live worker or reviewer
335	   rerun for acknowledgement; preserve worker reports and verdicts.
336	3. Repairs require worker investigation without candidate mutation, distinct FO
337	   `fix` authorization through the runtime's addressable-worker boundary, then
338	   independent validation. Without that authorization, hold.
339	4. Scope, value, threshold, tolerance, risk-acceptance and acceptance-criteria
340	   changes require the Captain. Material findings cannot use the record-only lane;
341	   hold/route-for-decision forbids repair and reviewer rerun.
342	5. A round is one verdict of an external reviewer of the delivery on the PR head (Codex
343	   on the PR, RoboRev or another); FO counts rounds and records the count in the
344	   committed gate summary. A reviewer that a listed extension covers is read the way its
345	   `EXTENSION.md` says (`## Extensions`). A finding assessed Material, or labelled P1 by
346	   the reviewer, blocks in every round: a reviewer P1 is fixed and revalidated, or
347	   waived by the Captain with the reason recorded (step 4). For an external reviewer
348	   that has no P1 label, its highest severity level counts as P1 (e.g. RoboRev). Rounds
349	   1 and 2 follow steps 1 to 4. From round 3 a finding that is neither does not start a
350	   repair cycle: FO declines it in the committed gate summary, naming the finding, and
351	   files it as a new backlog task with `spacedock new` whose body carries the finding
352	   and the decline reason, or names the backlog task that already holds it when a later
353	   round repeats it; it never enters an open task's Scope. The terminal gate lists each
354	   such task.
355	
356	Rejection routing carries evidence, classifications, authorized dispositions and assignment
357	without re-triage.
358	
359	Materiality and ownership are independent. Owned Material is eligible for an
360	FO-authorized fix; out-of-scope Material holds as Needs decision. Deferred risk
361	or Polish may use the recorded FO decline above within existing risk acceptance.
362	
363	A Needs decision put to the Captain at a gate carries FO's recommendation. His
364	plain approval accepts that recommendation only when the gate question says so,
365	for example "approving accepts the recommendation for D2; say if you object".
366	Without that sentence a decision he did not address stays open: FO records its
367	handling as FO's reading, never as his ruling, and asks him.
368	
369	A decision an accepted ADR already settles is not asked again: FO applies it and states it
370	in the gate summary as `Precedent: ADR <number> — 「<that ADR's Words line>」`, and the
371	Captain may reopen it. An ADR with no Words line is quoted by the decision sentence it
372	applies, as `Precedent: ADR <number> (no Words line) — 「<that sentence>」`. Authority, a gate approval, a merge, an outward-facing action, an
373	irreversible change and money are always asked, whatever an ADR says, and an ADR on one
374	of them is never a `Precedent:` line.
375	
376	A Captain ruling is his reply to the question it settles, given after that question
377	was put. FO never records as his ruling: silence on a decision the question did not
378	state approval accepts, consent he gave earlier to a different question, or a choice
379	he raised but did not make. FO answers a question the Captain asks at a gate before
380	dispatching on it, and returns a choice he raised to him rather than to a worker.
381	
382	When the Captain chooses differently from the recommendation, FO writes
383	`Override: recommended <option>; Captain chose <option>; area: <area>` in the gate
384	resolution reason, so later workers find past rulings with `git grep 'Override:'` in
385	the state checkout.
386	
387	## Decision records
388	
389	The implementation worker writes one ADR file per decision by its stage principles.
390	Validation runs `python3 <package>/scripts/adr_lint.py docs/adr --since <base>`, which
391	requires every record the candidate added or changed, plus `--require <numbers>` for
392	each `ADR:` number the task's `## Number guards` reserves and any number the
393	implementation report names; exit 1 or a missing record returns through the existing
394	feedback route, and exit 2 is a configuration error that returns to FO.
395	
396	## FO steps: decision records
397	
398	A ruling settled at a gate, in a worker report, or mid-stage feedback — a rule about
399	the product, a constraint, or a direction later work must respect — is landed as an
400	ADR before the next gate is presented, at latest by the terminal approval. A ruling
401	that governs only this task's own work stays in the task. A design names an ADR
402	by its ruling and the file's short title, with no number; FO reserves the number when
403	it dispatches implementation (Number guards) and the implementation worker writes
404	`docs/adr/<reserved number>-<short-title>.md`. FO confirms the validation ADR lint
405	passes before presenting the gate. A deferred user-facing capability belongs on
406	the product's journey map, not here.
407	
408	## Captain amendments
409	
410	A change the Captain makes to what he has accepted, whether at a gate approval,
411	between gates or at a validation gate, is an amendment. A change he asks for
412	while the gate that would accept it is still open is not one: he calls `revise`; at a stage
413	with no `feedback-to` that dispatches a worker, that stage's worker reworks it; at a stage
414	whose gate has a `feedback-to`, the revision goes to that target and the stage's worker
415	re-reviews it; and at `backlog`, which dispatches no worker, FO revises the recorded outcome,
416	scope or budget, or asks the proposal's author to.
417	
418	FO appends one entry per amendment to the task's `## Captain amendments` section and
419	changes nothing else in it. FO adds no words of its own and does not move or rewrite a criterion:
420	
421	```
422	## Captain amendments
423	
424	### Amendment 1 — <date>, <gate or chat>
425	Captain: 「<his words, verbatim>」 (where he said them)
426	Asked: <the question or proposal he answered, verbatim, or the commit holding it>
427	Supersedes: <acceptance-criterion ids, or none> <optional: "(no replacement: <why>)">
428	Design: <optional: the design paragraph it overrides>
429	```
430	
431	`Asked:` is required when his words do not name what they settle, such as 「同意第三點」. FO
432	names the amendment in the next dispatch's checklist. That worker (implementation, the
433	repair worker on a feedback route, or the worker of the stage a task is sent back to)
434	moves each superseded criterion's block verbatim from `## Acceptance criteria` into its
435	entry under a `Superseded text:` line, writes any replacement as a new `**AC-N**` under
436	a fresh id that says "Amended by Captain, amendment N", and never reuses an id. A
437	superseded criterion and the design paragraph named by `Design:` are withdrawn; evidence
438	and the Captain's acceptance script follow `## Acceptance criteria` plus the entries.
439	
440	Sending an approved task back to an earlier stage, such as a design redo a release
441	review asks for, is the Captain's decision and is recorded as an amendment whose
442	`Design:` names what is redone; FO then runs `spacedock status --workflow-dir <dir>
443	--set <slug> status=<stage>`, and that stage's gate is approved again before the task
444	moves on.
445	
446	`python3 <package>/scripts/design_surfaces.py check <task>`, run by implementation and
447	validation, prints each defect and exits 1; repair findings return through feedback. It cannot see a skipped record or
448	move, or FO's words in `Design:`.

450	## Affected documents
451	
452	Implementation runs `python3 <package>/scripts/doc_impact.py <base> <candidate>`
453	and records, for each listed document, `updated` or `unaffected: <reason>` in its
454	stage report; validation reruns it at the candidate and checks every listed
455	document carries one. Make the update itself by the retained-document practices in

458	## Number guards
459	
460	Applies when the task's `Surfaces:` includes `db`, or the task lands an ADR, including one first required by a ruling in a worker report or mid-stage feedback, whose number FO reserves before the next dispatch; the POC bullet below applies to every `poc` task.
461	`python3 <package>/scripts/number_guards.py --help` lists the flags and rules R1 to R6;
462	`trunk:`, `migrations-path:` and `adr-path:` (default `docs/adr`) come from this README's frontmatter.
463	
464	- **Applied.** `check` freezes a migration in a commit recorded `Applied at:` (R2).
465	  `Applied: none as of <sha>` records that
466	  nothing was pushed up to that commit; a validator that finds none of `Applied at:`,
467	  `Not applied:` or `Applied: none` reports the missing record to FO instead of
468	  re-checking deploys. A task with no `Migration:` line owes none of these.
469	- **Check.** `python3 <package>/scripts/number_guards.py check --workflow-dir <workflow-dir> --task <task file>`
470	  runs at implementation exit, at validation and, after `git -C <repo> fetch`, on the PR
471	  head before FO asks for merge. Exit 2 is a configuration error, which returns to FO
472	  as a hold.
473	- **POC.** A task whose recorded `profile` is `poc` adds, edits and deletes no migration
474	  file and reserves no number. A `FAIL R6` crosses the POC boundary
475	  (a schema change persists across sessions): the worker records
476	  `boundary-crossed: persistent-state` naming the path, and the task is not repaired in
477	  place.
478	
479	## FO steps: number guards
480	
481	- **Reserve.** Before an implementation dispatch, FO runs `git -C <repo> fetch`, then
482	  `python3 <package>/scripts/number_guards.py reserve --kind migration|adr --workflow-dir <workflow-dir> --repo <repo> --task <task file>`
483	  once per kind the task needs, when the implementation dispatch is built and not
484	  earlier; a task holds one number per kind, and a task needing a second ADR or
485	  migration returns to FO. FO records each printed `Migration: NNNN` /
486	  `ADR: NNNN` line under `## Number guards` in the task and repeats the lines as
487	  dispatch scope notes.
488	- **Applied.** Before any push of a candidate to a persistent shared non-production
489	  environment (a database branch, or a separate hosting project such as a staging
490	  project whose database is that project's own production database), FO records `Applied at: <environment> <sha>`
491	  for the commit being pushed. When the push is rejected or the
492	  deploy is confirmed not to have run for that commit (the push's non-zero output,
493	  or the environment's own deploy record showing no deploy of it), FO replaces that
494	  one line with `Not applied: <environment> <sha> - <evidence>` and the migration is
495	  no longer frozen. Without that confirmation the line stays and the migration counts
496	  as applied. When FO dispatches validation and nothing was pushed for the task, FO
497	  records `Applied: none as of <candidate sha>`, so a task with neither line has a
498	  skipped record. A task with no `Migration:` line records no `Applied:` line.
499	- **POC marker.** FO presents the `boundary-crossed: persistent-state` marker at the
500	  validation gate. Without `migrations-path:` a db task exits 2 and a POC is not guarded;
501	  `none` declares no migration files.
502	- **Collision.** When two tasks hold one migration number (`check` reports R3 or R5 on
503	  the later candidate; nothing compares task files), the task whose migration is applied
504	  keeps it and the other, unapplied task renumbers, so no reset is needed. A migration
505	  counts as applied when its task has an `Applied at:` line or it is on the base branch;
506	  when both tasks are applied and neither is on the base branch, the one that merges
507	  first keeps the number. The renumbering task deletes its `Migration:` line, FO runs
508	  `reserve` again, and the task returns to implementation with the new number in its
509	  scope notes. When the renumbering task has an `Applied at:` line, its environment's
510	  database holds a migration no branch will carry, and FO holds for the Captain: a
511	  database branch is reset, and a shared non-production database that cannot be reset
512	  (a separate project's own database) is deleted and recreated by the Captain. FO then
513	  replaces the line with `Not applied: <environment> <sha> - database reset` so that
514	  `check` accepts the renumber. A branch database is reset through the provider's own API; `adoption.md` gives one
515	  provider's example. This step is documented, not wrapped in a tool.
516	
517	## Delivery authority
518	
519	The adopted `_mods/pr-merge.md` is the unmodified mod from the activated SD
520	package. Before delivery, confirm the file still matches the reviewed source
521	(or an explicitly approved project customization) and its merge hook is
522	registered. Missing/changed delivery configuration requires a hold: `merge: pr`
523	alone does not block SD's no-hook local-finalize route.
524	
525	Project and Captain authority constrain hook instructions: present the exact candidate and
526	PR body before authorized push/create; create a Draft PR where required, and request ready
527	only after the required CI is green. Where CI skips drafts, FO marks the PR ready under
528	the Captain's authority and waits for those jobs before asking for merge. Approval of a
529	validation gate is not permission to push, create or merge a PR, except as follows. FO's
530	delivery gate question says approval also covers later external-review rounds on the same
531	PR, merging the full head `<package>/scripts/delivery_gate.py check` passes, with
532	`--match-head-commit` set to it, unless he says he merges or holds, and removing its
533	clean, pushed worktree. Under that approval, a repair whose validation passes with no
534	Material or Needs decision finding is recorded by FO
535	(`gate record --actor agent:first-officer` with `--conn-quote` and `--conn-source` naming
536	his approval) and pushed to that PR's branch, after confirming the pushed commit is the
537	candidate the report names. A rejected repair, a Needs decision and a scope change go to
538	him. Preserve manual merge authority. Do not invoke local fallback, push the trunk, merge,
539	or clean up an owned worktree unless the specific action is authorized. An upstream hook's
540	default fallback is not that grant. A failure holds delivery pending an explicit choice.
541	
542	Under the Captain's grant quoted in its dispatch, the implementation worker opens the task's
543	Draft PR before validation; that grant stands in for a presented body. Observe the actual
544	repository-qualified PR merge before recording its landed sentinel and running SD merge guard
545	to finalize/archive. Where `learn` is listed, the sentinel waits for a committed observer report.
546	CI green, PR creation, gate approval and a locally manufactured sentinel do not prove merge.
547	FO's startup and idle steps are in `_mods/kc-dev-flow-2.md`, copied from `<package>/references/sd/mods/`.
548	
549	Before the validation `gate prepare`, FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/delivery_gate.py question <task> --text-file <question file> --summary-file <summary file>`; nonzero holds preparation. The summary declares `External rounds: N` and the configured second-reviewer outcome. Use that summary unchanged; callers omitting `--summary-file` retain combined-text checks.
550	
551	Before merging or asking, FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/delivery_gate.py check <task>
552	--pr <owner/repo>#<N> --text-file <question and summary>`; exit 1 or 2 holds the ask, as does a head other than the latest `Candidate:`; FO shows the Captain what it printed.
553	
554	`merge guard --rework` supersedes the approval and routes the task back, but its
555	help names no commit or publish step, unlike the archive path. After it, FO runs
556	`spacedock state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`, publishes, and reads the task
557	back from the state remote before dispatching the repair; otherwise durable state
558	can still show the task awaiting merge.
559	
560	## Extensions
561	
562	Extensions are optional accessories in `<package>/extensions/<name>/`, each described by
563	its `EXTENSION.md`: what it needs, the stage or FO step it joins, the instruction it
564	adds, how its result is read, and what happens when it cannot run. This README's
565	frontmatter `extensions:` lists the ones this repository uses; an unlisted extension is
566	not probed and adds nothing. For a listed extension FO follows its `EXTENSION.md`: at a
567	worker dispatch of its stage FO adds its instruction line to the scope notes, and at its
568	FO step FO reads the result as the file says. A listed extension that cannot run, or that FO does not request because a ruling says not to, is
569	reported as `<name> not run: <reason>` in the stage report or gate summary, and never
570	counts as a clean result. A merge ask names each listed reviewer that was not read, and
571	the Captain decides. Where two remote reviewers are listed, frontmatter `second-reviewer:`
572	names the one that joins only when a trigger holds: the task's `Surfaces:` include `db`,
573	its profile is `prod`, a dispatch said its design is hard to reverse, the change touches authority,
574	approval, merge or review rules, or the Captain asks. FO records `second reviewer: <name>
575	because <trigger>` or `second reviewer: not triggered` in the gate summary, and an
576	untriggered second reviewer is not named as unread.
577	
578	## Workflow State
579	
580	The README and `_mods` stay in the code repository; mutable task state lives in

# Development workflow
<!-- kc-dev-flow-2 0.33.1 x-release-please-version -->

This is the adopted workflow's authority for SD stages and task schema. Resolve
its absolute directory and retain `--workflow-dir` on SD commands, including
worker reads and recovery. Skills guide work; SD owns dispatch, gates and state.

## File Naming

Each task is a flat `<slug>.md` file in the resolved state checkout. Keep existing
IDs and tasks in their recorded workflow; new work does not migrate old work.

## Schema

Record `title`, `status`, `variant: kc-dev-flow-2`, and the user's selected
`profile`; `id` is optional under `id-style: slug`. The five-stage route accepts
`pilot` or `prod`; the POC adaptation
removes ideation from both frontmatter and Stages and accepts `poc` only.
Before admission and dispatch, FO holds unknown/mismatched profiles;
SD does not enforce this rule. Preserve approved outcome and scope.
New seeds require non-empty `Non-goals:`, `Budget:` and `Stop condition:` lines
under `## Scope` or matching level-two sections. Replay counts do not enforce
these on existing tasks. Use bold **AC-N** declarations with individual evidence clauses.

## Batch gates

A Captain-approved batch covers one release slice or theme. Recover members from accepted scopes/questions, without another list. Unclear membership holds presentation; membership changes or splits need his decision. Incompatible stage graphs need an explicitly approved split.

At each next gate, wait for every member's sufficient committed evidence, then present the batch in one sitting. Early finishers prompt no decision. Continue authorized repairs/validation. A blocker needing Captain authority gets one exception question naming the member and effect. Do not manufacture hold resolutions.

`<package>/scripts/pr_watch.py tasks` sitting hints remain subject to this boundary; stage alone joins neither unrelated tasks nor incomplete batches. Unbatched tasks retain ordinary gates.

When requested, chief-engineer reviews the complete package/process batch before briefing bindings; engineering-reviewer handles contested hard-to-reverse claims. Give committed task files/artifact links, not FO's suspicions/conclusions. Record reviewer/model/evidence; use a different family from all workers or ask the Captain. Review advises, without approval authority.

## Stages

Stage workers run on the workflow's default model.
`kc-dev-flow-2:chief-engineer`, `kc-dev-flow-2:engineering-reviewer` and
`kc-dev-flow-2:observer` run on the model and reasoning their agent files declare, never
a cheaper one. Record chief-engineer and engineering-reviewer calls under `## FO alignment` as
`Reviewer: <agent> <model> <date> — <question>`; `<package>/scripts/role_triggers.py` lists calls owed.

`concurrency` limits only what `status --next` proposes. A feedback-reflow repair and an
FO fix authorized under Review-finding disposition step 3 are dispatched at once in the
entity's own worktree, after the existing overlap check against running worktrees; they
do not wait for another entity's worker in the same stage. The validation recheck of
that repair or fix does not wait for another entity's worker either, but it is
dispatched only after the repair or fix has completed and committed its candidate, so
the validator reads the bytes that will be delivered. A repair that outgrows what its
assignment names returns to FO as a scope change.

FO resolves `<package>` in this workflow from the `Package root:` line of
`kc-dev-flow-2:dev`. Before each worker dispatch FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/package_version.py
<this README>`; exit 1 means the session loaded an older package than this README was synced
from, and FO holds the dispatch until the session runs the newer one. FO also runs
`python3 <package>/scripts/workflow_checkout.py <this README>`, which compares this file with
`origin/<trunk>`'s: exit 1 means they differ, exit 2 that it could not compare, and FO
holds the dispatch and shows the Captain what the script printed. Every worker dispatch FO builds carries that absolute path as a
`Package root: <absolute path>` line in its scope notes (`--scope-notes-file`), which
land in the dispatch file the worker reads first. Those scope notes, and every follow-up
message to a live worker, also carry ``Send your completion message to `main` (the README's Dispatch
facts: `team-lead` is not registered here).``: the builder's completion block names `team-lead`, and a
worker that skips the stage-definition fetch does not see the Signal fact. FO saves those scope notes, the
checklist, the model it dispatches on and the SHA it dispatches from as
`<task>/dispatch/<stage>-<cycle>.md` in the state checkout (for validation a
`Candidate: <full head SHA>` line per head validated),
committed with that dispatch's `spacedock state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`, so
the instruction a worker followed outlives the session that wrote it; FO runs
`python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py <task folder>` before committing and fixes each part it lists. A follow-up
message to a worker FO resumes is a dispatch too, with the same check and a checklist of the items that message asks, never a pointer to another record.
After each worker report, before advancing or preparing its gate, FO runs
`python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py --coverage <task> --stage <stage>`; nonzero holds that task.
This check does not observe unrecorded messages.
A checklist or scope-notes line that names a package script writes
`<package>/scripts/NAME.py` with the absolute root substituted, never the bare script
name; before `dispatch build`, FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py --names <record>`
on the saved record and rewrites each name it lists. When `status --set` refuses to leave a stage, run `spacedock status --workflow-dir
<dir> --read <task> --stage <stage> --checklist`, return any line it reports as neither
DONE nor SKIPPED to the worker with the request to append a complete new report under the same heading, ending in a Summary that supersedes the earlier one, and do not edit the worker's report. The refusal itself
does not say why; other causes are a missing evidence line or Summary and an uncommitted
report.

### `backlog`

The user selects the compatible profile and approves outcome, scope and budget.
FO records the choice; this boundary has no worker or placeholder report. FO
also records, under a `## FO alignment` heading in the task file, whether FO
direction alignment with the Captain is needed before the next declared stage
and why; a
stated reason is the whole record when not needed. On the five-stage route, FO
also records a `Surfaces:` line under the same heading: any of `ui`, `db`,
or `none`, read from the change surface rather than the diff, and next to it
a `Visible change:` line: one sentence on what a user sees or operates
differently, or `Visible change: none`.

- **Gate content:** Show the selected variant/profile, proposed outcome, scope,
  exclusions and evidence needed before the next declared stage starts, the
  `## FO alignment` need and reason, and the recorded `Surfaces:` and
  `Visible change:` lines on the five-stage route.
- **Seed check:** On the five-stage route, before `gate prepare`, FO runs
  `python3 <package>/scripts/design_surfaces.py check --seed <task>` and holds the
  gate until it exits 0. An FO that skips this step still dispatches; no runtime hook blocks it.
- **Release review:** Applies to a task that belongs to a release on a journey map
  (`journey`, `journey-release`, `journey-story`); a task with no release, such as a
  bug, infrastructure or workflow maintenance, is outside it. Four signals: (1) a task
  admitted into a release; (2) a Captain scope ruling that moves a story or task into
  or out of a release or changes the goal of the release, a story or a task; (3) a UAT
  failure that crosses two or more tasks; (4) a batch about to enter implementation. Signals 1 and 2 only mark the
  release changed: FO names the release and the signal in the task's `## FO alignment`
  reason. A task whose `journey-story` is already on the map in that release passes with
  that one check and marks nothing when, since its latest `Release review:` line, the
  journey file still holds the same story ids and the same release and story `goal`
  text and no Captain ruling has changed the goal of the release, a story or a task.
  A changed goal is signal 2 although no story id moved; FO marks the release
  changed in that task's `## FO alignment` reason. Signal 4 is the single checkpoint: at the first
  implementation dispatch for a release marked changed, FO dispatches a fresh worker
  with kc-journey-map's `review-release` mode, then splits tasks from its output; an
  unchanged release proceeds. One review covers every change since the last. Signal 3
  runs the review at once. FO writes no map and no candidate; the Captain accepts
  membership in conversation or at this gate. FO records under `## FO alignment` either
  `Release review: <journey>/<release-id> at <journey-file commit>` or
  `Release review: not needed: <reason>`. When FO approves
  a task into a release story at this gate it sets the three fields with
  `spacedock status --workflow-dir <dir> --set <task> journey=<the map's journey: value> journey-release=<id> journey-story=<id>`;
  a worker never edits frontmatter. Where the adopter tracks completion with
  kc-journey-progress, FO also writes `journey-required-tasks` (full task ids) and
  `journey-mapping-complete: true` on one task per story at the review's split step.
  When signal 2 moves a task out of a release, FO clears its release fields with
  `spacedock status --workflow-dir <dir> --set <task> journey= journey-release= journey-story= journey-required-tasks= journey-mapping-complete=`

### `done`

Consuming a terminal gate approval is not completion (`spacedock merge guard --help`);
a live run requires the declared delivery evidence and successful `merge guard` with
an explicit verdict. Apply Delivery authority below; a pending PR or missing hook is
not completion.

## Dispatch facts

- **Team:** You are one worker in a team completing the project goal; your stage
  and handoff serve that goal. Before substantial work or retrying a failure,
  check this task's prior reports, linked sibling tasks and PRs, and relevant
  workflow state: did someone already do this, hit this, or own it now? If your
  environment cannot run a required checklist check, tell FO before building
  work that depends on it. Ask FO early about overlapping ownership, repeated
  failures, missing authority or evidence, or infeasible targets. Give checked
  sources, findings, attempts and the specific question. With a mid-run FO
  channel, pause dependent work and continue safe independent work; without
  one, end your turn with that handback instead of waiting. Never answer your
  own or your reviewers' permission requests; route them to FO. FO coordinates
  peers and decisions; do not message peers or change others' work.
- **Signal:** send the completion message once, to the first officer by the name
  your session lists as addressable (`main` under Claude Code dispatch). The
  completion block's `team-lead` is Spacedock's default and is not registered
  there (spacedock-dev/spacedock #523, #608); do not try it first and do not
  describe a fallback in the report.
- **Package:** `<package>` in stage text is the `Package root:` line of the
  kc-dev-flow-2 skill you loaded; your dispatch's scope notes state the same path,
  and if they differ, use the skill's. Run package scripts only from it; never
  search the filesystem, `/tmp` or another install for them.
- **Secrets:** `<wrapper>` is the only route to a development secret: run a
  command that needs one as `<wrapper> <command>`. Never read or print a value.
  If a guard refuses a command that only mentions a secret-reading tool, rephrase
  it; do not split, encode or wrap the command to pass the guard.

## Review-finding disposition

Before repair authorization, product bytes and the recorded candidate revision stay
unchanged. Read-only inspection, non-mutating reproductions, existing tests and
throwaway-checkout probes are allowed. Report/gate commits may advance repository
HEAD without changing the candidate. Validators recommend `PASSED` or `REJECTED`;
new findings or changed evidence re-enter this checkpoint.

The four evidence fields are released user and normal workflow; observable harm;
affected value acceptance criterion or non-negotiable boundary; and trigger
evidence. Field 3 uses `value-ac[AC-N]`, `captain-ruling[YYYY-MM-DD]`, or
`contract[repo/relative/path#anchor]` plus a nonblank claim. `none:` with a rationale
does not establish Material.

- **Material:** all four fields establish supported-workflow harm to a protected
  boundary or value acceptance criterion.
- **Deferred risk:** hypothetical, unsupported, unobserved or unpromised trigger;
  record what would make it material.
- **Polish:** no current user-visible loss or protected boundary is at risk.
- **Needs decision:** the task cannot own the scope, product or compatibility call.

A `Follow-up:` line in Scope is not accepted scope by itself: the first stage of the
receiving task to meet it assesses it against its stated reason and earlier rulings. It builds the line only when the change alters no behaviour that an
accepted criterion, a Captain ruling or a journey contract relies on; otherwise it
returns the line to FO as a Needs decision. It records which, and why.
A finding FO declined in a committed gate summary or under `### FO declines` is settled:
a later validator does not report it again unless the candidate changes the lines or the
evidence the decline names, or new evidence would make it Material.

## FO steps: review findings

Apply this checkpoint to findings from implementation, validation, detached audits,
consequential FO quick work and rejected gates.

1. Reviewers observe; workers' classifications and `actor:ensign` Resolutions are
   advisory. Preserve findings and assess the four evidence fields above, separating
   materiality, ownership and disposition. Missing required evidence or unresolved
   classification requires investigation or hold.
2. Within approved boundaries, FO may explicitly decline evidenced Deferred risk or
   Polish in the existing committed gate summary, naming the finding, reason, candidate
   revision and the lines or evidence it rests on. When that summary is already
   consumed, FO writes the decline under `### FO declines` in the task file, committed
   with `spacedock state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`, and the terminal gate
   lists each entry there. This FO-authored decision requires no live worker or reviewer
   rerun for acknowledgement; preserve worker reports and verdicts.
3. Repairs require worker investigation without candidate mutation, distinct FO
   `fix` authorization through the runtime's addressable-worker boundary, then
   independent validation. Without that authorization, hold.
4. Scope, value, threshold, tolerance, risk-acceptance and acceptance-criteria
   changes require the Captain. Material findings cannot use the record-only lane;
   hold/route-for-decision forbids repair and reviewer rerun.
5. A round is one verdict of an external reviewer of the delivery on the PR head (Codex
   on the PR, RoboRev or another); FO counts rounds and records the count in the
   committed gate summary. A reviewer that a listed extension covers is read the way its
   `EXTENSION.md` says (`## Extensions`). A finding assessed Material, or labelled P1 by
   the reviewer, blocks in every round: a reviewer P1 is fixed and revalidated, or
   waived by the Captain with the reason recorded (step 4). For an external reviewer
   that has no P1 label, its highest severity level counts as P1 (e.g. RoboRev). Rounds
   1 and 2 follow steps 1 to 4. From round 3 a finding that is neither does not start a
   repair cycle: FO declines it in the committed gate summary, naming the finding, and
   files it as a new backlog task with `spacedock new` whose body carries the finding
   and the decline reason, or names the backlog task that already holds it when a later
   round repeats it; it never enters an open task's Scope. The terminal gate lists each
   such task.

Rejection routing carries evidence, classifications, authorized dispositions and assignment
without re-triage.

Materiality and ownership are independent. Owned Material is eligible for an
FO-authorized fix; out-of-scope Material holds as Needs decision. Deferred risk
or Polish may use the recorded FO decline above within existing risk acceptance.

A Needs decision put to the Captain at a gate carries FO's recommendation. His
plain approval accepts that recommendation only when the gate question says so,
for example "approving accepts the recommendation for D2; say if you object".
Without that sentence a decision he did not address stays open: FO records its
handling as FO's reading, never as his ruling, and asks him.

A decision an accepted ADR already settles is not asked again: FO applies it and states it
in the gate summary as `Precedent: ADR <number> — 「<that ADR's Words line>」`, and the
Captain may reopen it. An ADR with no Words line is quoted by the decision sentence it
applies, as `Precedent: ADR <number> (no Words line) — 「<that sentence>」`. Authority, a gate approval, a merge, an outward-facing action, an
irreversible change and money are always asked, whatever an ADR says, and an ADR on one
of them is never a `Precedent:` line.

A Captain ruling is his reply to the question it settles, given after that question
was put. FO never records as his ruling: silence on a decision the question did not
state approval accepts, consent he gave earlier to a different question, or a choice
he raised but did not make. FO answers a question the Captain asks at a gate before
dispatching on it, and returns a choice he raised to him rather than to a worker.

When the Captain chooses differently from the recommendation, FO writes
`Override: recommended <option>; Captain chose <option>; area: <area>` in the gate
resolution reason, so later workers find past rulings with `git grep 'Override:'` in
the state checkout.

## Decision records

The implementation worker writes one ADR file per decision by its stage principles.
Validation runs `python3 <package>/scripts/adr_lint.py docs/adr --since <base>`, which
requires every record the candidate added or changed, plus `--require <numbers>` for
each `ADR:` number the task's `## Number guards` reserves and any number the
implementation report names; exit 1 or a missing record returns through the existing
feedback route, and exit 2 is a configuration error that returns to FO.

## FO steps: decision records

A ruling settled at a gate, in a worker report, or mid-stage feedback — a rule about
the product, a constraint, or a direction later work must respect — is landed as an
ADR before the next gate is presented, at latest by the terminal approval. A ruling
that governs only this task's own work stays in the task. A design names an ADR
by its ruling and the file's short title, with no number; FO reserves the number when
it dispatches implementation (Number guards) and the implementation worker writes
`docs/adr/<reserved number>-<short-title>.md`. FO confirms the validation ADR lint
passes before presenting the gate. A deferred user-facing capability belongs on
the product's journey map, not here.

## Captain amendments

A change the Captain makes to what he has accepted, whether at a gate approval,
between gates or at a validation gate, is an amendment. A change he asks for
while the gate that would accept it is still open is not one: he calls `revise`; at a stage
with no `feedback-to` that dispatches a worker, that stage's worker reworks it; at a stage
whose gate has a `feedback-to`, the revision goes to that target and the stage's worker
re-reviews it; and at `backlog`, which dispatches no worker, FO revises the recorded outcome,
scope or budget, or asks the proposal's author to.

FO appends one entry per amendment to the task's `## Captain amendments` section and
changes nothing else in it. FO adds no words of its own and does not move or rewrite a criterion:

```
## Captain amendments

### Amendment 1 — <date>, <gate or chat>
Captain: 「<his words, verbatim>」 (where he said them)
Asked: <the question or proposal he answered, verbatim, or the commit holding it>
Supersedes: <acceptance-criterion ids, or none> <optional: "(no replacement: <why>)">
Design: <optional: the design paragraph it overrides>
```

`Asked:` is required when his words do not name what they settle, such as 「同意第三點」. FO
names the amendment in the next dispatch's checklist. That worker (implementation, the
repair worker on a feedback route, or the worker of the stage a task is sent back to)
moves each superseded criterion's block verbatim from `## Acceptance criteria` into its
entry under a `Superseded text:` line, writes any replacement as a new `**AC-N**` under
a fresh id that says "Amended by Captain, amendment N", and never reuses an id. A
superseded criterion and the design paragraph named by `Design:` are withdrawn; evidence
and the Captain's acceptance script follow `## Acceptance criteria` plus the entries.

Sending an approved task back to an earlier stage, such as a design redo a release
review asks for, is the Captain's decision and is recorded as an amendment whose
`Design:` names what is redone; FO then runs `spacedock status --workflow-dir <dir>
--set <slug> status=<stage>`, and that stage's gate is approved again before the task
moves on.

`python3 <package>/scripts/design_surfaces.py check <task>`, run by implementation and
validation, prints each defect and exits 1; repair findings return through feedback. It cannot see a skipped record or
move, or FO's words in `Design:`.

## Affected documents

Implementation runs `python3 <package>/scripts/doc_impact.py <base> <candidate>`
and records, for each listed document, `updated` or `unaffected: <reason>` in its
stage report; validation reruns it at the candidate and checks every listed
document carries one. Make the update itself by the retained-document practices in
the package's `references/retained-documents.md`.

## Number guards

Applies when the task's `Surfaces:` includes `db`, or the task lands an ADR, including one first required by a ruling in a worker report or mid-stage feedback, whose number FO reserves before the next dispatch; the POC bullet below applies to every `poc` task.
`python3 <package>/scripts/number_guards.py --help` lists the flags and rules R1 to R6;
`trunk:`, `migrations-path:` and `adr-path:` (default `docs/adr`) come from this README's frontmatter.

- **Applied.** `check` freezes a migration in a commit recorded `Applied at:` (R2).
  `Applied: none as of <sha>` records that
  nothing was pushed up to that commit; a validator that finds none of `Applied at:`,
  `Not applied:` or `Applied: none` reports the missing record to FO instead of
  re-checking deploys. A task with no `Migration:` line owes none of these.
- **Check.** `python3 <package>/scripts/number_guards.py check --workflow-dir <workflow-dir> --task <task file>`
  runs at implementation exit, at validation and, after `git -C <repo> fetch`, on the PR
  head before FO asks for merge. Exit 2 is a configuration error, which returns to FO
  as a hold.
- **POC.** A task whose recorded `profile` is `poc` adds, edits and deletes no migration
  file and reserves no number. A `FAIL R6` crosses the POC boundary
  (a schema change persists across sessions): the worker records
  `boundary-crossed: persistent-state` naming the path, and the task is not repaired in
  place.

## FO steps: number guards

- **Reserve.** Before an implementation dispatch, FO runs `git -C <repo> fetch`, then
  `python3 <package>/scripts/number_guards.py reserve --kind migration|adr --workflow-dir <workflow-dir> --repo <repo> --task <task file>`
  once per kind the task needs, when the implementation dispatch is built and not
  earlier; a task holds one number per kind, and a task needing a second ADR or
  migration returns to FO. FO records each printed `Migration: NNNN` /
  `ADR: NNNN` line under `## Number guards` in the task and repeats the lines as
  dispatch scope notes.
- **Applied.** Before any push of a candidate to a persistent shared non-production
  environment (a database branch, or a separate hosting project such as a staging
  project whose database is that project's own production database), FO records `Applied at: <environment> <sha>`
  for the commit being pushed. When the push is rejected or the
  deploy is confirmed not to have run for that commit (the push's non-zero output,
  or the environment's own deploy record showing no deploy of it), FO replaces that
  one line with `Not applied: <environment> <sha> - <evidence>` and the migration is
  no longer frozen. Without that confirmation the line stays and the migration counts
  as applied. When FO dispatches validation and nothing was pushed for the task, FO
  records `Applied: none as of <candidate sha>`, so a task with neither line has a
  skipped record. A task with no `Migration:` line records no `Applied:` line.
- **POC marker.** FO presents the `boundary-crossed: persistent-state` marker at the
  validation gate. Without `migrations-path:` a db task exits 2 and a POC is not guarded;
  `none` declares no migration files.
- **Collision.** When two tasks hold one migration number (`check` reports R3 or R5 on
  the later candidate; nothing compares task files), the task whose migration is applied
  keeps it and the other, unapplied task renumbers, so no reset is needed. A migration
  counts as applied when its task has an `Applied at:` line or it is on the base branch;
  when both tasks are applied and neither is on the base branch, the one that merges
  first keeps the number. The renumbering task deletes its `Migration:` line, FO runs
  `reserve` again, and the task returns to implementation with the new number in its
  scope notes. When the renumbering task has an `Applied at:` line, its environment's
  database holds a migration no branch will carry, and FO holds for the Captain: a
  database branch is reset, and a shared non-production database that cannot be reset
  (a separate project's own database) is deleted and recreated by the Captain. FO then
  replaces the line with `Not applied: <environment> <sha> - database reset` so that
  `check` accepts the renumber. A branch database is reset through the provider's own API; `adoption.md` gives one
  provider's example. This step is documented, not wrapped in a tool.

## Delivery authority

The adopted `_mods/pr-merge.md` is the unmodified mod from the activated SD
package. Before delivery, confirm the file still matches the reviewed source
(or an explicitly approved project customization) and its merge hook is
registered. Missing/changed delivery configuration requires a hold: `merge: pr`
alone does not block SD's no-hook local-finalize route.

Project and Captain authority constrain hook instructions: present the exact candidate and
PR body before authorized push/create; create a Draft PR where required, and request ready
only after the required CI is green. Where CI skips drafts, FO marks the PR ready under
the Captain's authority and waits for those jobs before asking for merge. Approval of a
validation gate is not permission to push, create or merge a PR, except as follows. FO's
delivery gate question says approval also covers later external-review rounds on the same
PR, merging the full head `<package>/scripts/delivery_gate.py check` passes, with
`--match-head-commit` set to it, unless he says he merges or holds, and removing its
clean, pushed worktree. Under that approval, a repair whose validation passes with no
Material or Needs decision finding is recorded by FO
(`gate record --actor agent:first-officer` with `--conn-quote` and `--conn-source` naming
his approval) and pushed to that PR's branch, after confirming the pushed commit is the
candidate the report names. A rejected repair, a Needs decision and a scope change go to
him. Preserve manual merge authority. Do not invoke local fallback, push the trunk, merge,
or clean up an owned worktree unless the specific action is authorized. An upstream hook's
default fallback is not that grant. A failure holds delivery pending an explicit choice.

Under the Captain's grant quoted in its dispatch, the implementation worker opens the task's
Draft PR before validation; that grant stands in for a presented body. Observe the actual
repository-qualified PR merge before recording its landed sentinel and running SD merge guard
to finalize/archive. Where `learn` is listed, the sentinel waits for a committed observer report.
CI green, PR creation, gate approval and a locally manufactured sentinel do not prove merge.
FO's startup and idle steps are in `_mods/kc-dev-flow-2.md`, copied from `<package>/references/sd/mods/`.

Before the validation `gate prepare`, FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/delivery_gate.py question <task> --text-file <question file> --summary-file <summary file>`; nonzero holds preparation. The summary declares `External rounds: N` and the configured second-reviewer outcome. Use that summary unchanged; callers omitting `--summary-file` retain combined-text checks.

Before merging or asking, FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/delivery_gate.py check <task>
--pr <owner/repo>#<N> --text-file <question and summary>`; exit 1 or 2 holds the ask, as does a head other than the latest `Candidate:`; FO shows the Captain what it printed.

`merge guard --rework` supersedes the approval and routes the task back, but its
help names no commit or publish step, unlike the archive path. After it, FO runs
`spacedock state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`, publishes, and reads the task
back from the state remote before dispatching the repair; otherwise durable state
can still show the task awaiting merge.

## Extensions

Extensions are optional accessories in `<package>/extensions/<name>/`, each described by
its `EXTENSION.md`: what it needs, the stage or FO step it joins, the instruction it
adds, how its result is read, and what happens when it cannot run. This README's
frontmatter `extensions:` lists the ones this repository uses; an unlisted extension is
not probed and adds nothing. For a listed extension FO follows its `EXTENSION.md`: at a
worker dispatch of its stage FO adds its instruction line to the scope notes, and at its
FO step FO reads the result as the file says. A listed extension that cannot run, or that FO does not request because a ruling says not to, is
reported as `<name> not run: <reason>` in the stage report or gate summary, and never
counts as a clean result. A merge ask names each listed reviewer that was not read, and
the Captain decides. Where two remote reviewers are listed, frontmatter `second-reviewer:`
names the one that joins only when a trigger holds: the task's `Surfaces:` include `db`,
its profile is `prod`, a dispatch said its design is hard to reverse, the change touches authority,
approval, merge or review rules, or the Captain asks. FO records `second reviewer: <name>
because <trigger>` or `second reviewer: not triggered` in the gate summary, and an
untriggered second reviewer is not named as unread.

## Workflow State

The README and `_mods` stay in the code repository; mutable task state lives in
`.spacedock-state`, an ignored linked checkout of this workflow's distinct orphan
state branch. Commission/refit owns setup; a fresh clone uses SD state init.
POC uses independent validation in this variant, and special Production recovery
routes are not implemented.

FO commits task state only through SD commands (`gate record`, `state commit
<slug>`, each with `--workflow-dir <dir>`), never by staging the state checkout with
`git add -A` or `git add .`: a broad add sweeps a worker's uncommitted report into
another task's commit.

## Task Template

```markdown

id: <task-id>
title: <bounded outcome>
status: backlog
variant: kc-dev-flow-2
profile: <selected-profile>
merge: pr
worktree:
pr:
---

<Why this outcome matters.>

## Scope

<Approved outcome and scope.>
Non-goals: <exclusions>
Budget: <approved bound>
Stop condition: <when to return to the Captain>

## Acceptance criteria

**AC-1**: <Observable outcome.>
Verified by: <Reproducible evidence and its limits.>
```

Optional frontmatter, absent until used: `journey`, `journey-release` and
`journey-story`, set by FO at Release review (see `backlog`). A placeholder comment would sit beside the real values once
`status --set` filled them, so the template carries none.
